## Work completed in this continuation

[A6: almost-sure recovery without finite expected cost](A6-almost-sure-recovery-and-cost-v02.md) adds:

1. A source-grounded correction: Carter and Hawthorne do make local continuation claims, so the earlier draft understated its direct relevance.
2. A proof that unbounded transparency witness lengths plus independent sampling imply almost-sure, arbitrarily late availability of every fixed finite level.
3. An abstract threshold hierarchy in which first-order knowledge is available, second-order knowledge is attained almost surely, and its first attainment time has infinite expectation.
4. An explicit distinction between the proved formal separation and an unresolved dynamic epistemic realization.
5. An absorbing-walk calculation, checked against exhaustive enumeration through ten draws, and calibrated comparisons with Brown and Hong.

This is a stronger conditional note, not an originality-cleared philosophical breakthrough. The probability results are standard. The new work does not establish permission to inquire or refute the complete Carter–Hawthorne account.
